question: Does an externally prepared one-hot K4 root persist under free Q166 vertex-edge incidence flow?

objects.definition: x in R4,y in R6, free unit-metric skew incidence evolution

assumptions: A1 exogenous e0 one-hot preparation, y0=0
A2 free closed K4 vertex/edge truncation with H=I
A3 root readout by unique maximum signed amplitude or squared stock

technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Q166 current and positive quadratic stock balance
continuous dimensionless period pi, not finite modular clock

factor_origins: complete graph degree 3, one offdiagonal incidence overlap -1

clock_receipt.period_claim: pi in s for this prepared state

dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: e0 vertex, zero edge; closed boundary
dynamics_readout.conservation_and_sources: S=1, Q166 F_ie=2 B_ie x_i y_e, no reservoir
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: uniform vertex mode 1/4 and contrast mode frequency 2

known_targets: rooted geometry map requires one root
target_exposure.search_domain_and_budget: one minimal one-hot preparation and free generator
target_exposure.selection_criterion: first time unique amplitude/stock root fails

calculation_steps: BB^T=4I-J, with uniform kernel and 3-dimensional eigenvalue 4 subspace.
Root minus each other vertex is cos(2s); first amplitude tie s=pi/4.
Squared-stock difference is cos(2s)(1+cos(2s))/2; negative for -1<cos(2s)<0.
At s=pi/2, x=(-1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2), y=0, all vertex stocks 1/4.
S=1 and local Q166 continuity; full period pi gives zero net signed stock transfer.

result.exact_expression: first amplitude tie pi/4, free period pi, S=1; root stock difference c(1+c)/2
result.precision_and_error: analytic exact trigonometric solution; rational sample checks exact
result.scope: free 0/1 K4 unit-metric truncation and one-hot seed
result.physical_interpretation: no persistent amplitude-based root, not a physical friction result

verification.method: exact rational phase replay and analytic proof
verification.actual_result: PASS equations, stock/current balance, phase samples

counterexamples_and_failures: Fixed external one-hot contact label could persist despite free amplitudes; not supplied by this model.
Driven, masked, nonlinear or open-system dynamics may avoid the tie.
limitations: Free 0/1 truncation excludes faces and gate transitions.
No physical clock, material damping or measured force/angle.
next_discriminant: Sourced persistent contact register with exact stock/power accounting and physical readout.
